intro: The cabinet in the back corner of the arcade has been unplugged since 1987, and its faded table of initials still fills with new names overnight. Mrs. Okabe, who runs the place, keeps the cabinet's loose belongings — bent token trays, instruction cards, dead joysticks — in the pigeonholes behind the counter, each hole cut to fit exactly one item, so that a glance tells her what is missing and what has slipped in sideways. She files everything the same way, she says, because a thing that fits nowhere does not belong in her arcade. In chalk she marks the bottom of every hole that holds something, and the letters of those marks spell out a word she refuses to translate. The players say the initials on the cabinet last changed the night that word was finished.
echo: Once it meant a row of arches; now it means a row of glowing cabinets.

puzzles.title: Save State
puzzles.flavor: Fill in the blanks, literally. Some squares have been given to you for free.
hints: A nonogram (paint-by-numbers). The filled picture is the answer written in 5×5 block letters.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with A.

puzzles.title: Level 256
puzzles.flavor: Noughts and crosses, with a few stray dots where someone pressed too hard.
hints: Pigpen (Freemason's) cipher: A–I in a # grid, J–R the same with dots, S–V in an X, W–Z the X with dots.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with D.

puzzles.title: Up Up Down Down
puzzles.flavor: Julius would have read this before breakfast.

blocks.text: PXEE WHGX RHN FTR GHP PKBMX WHPG MAX PHKW ETLXKZNG TGW FHOX JNBXMER HG MH MAX GXQM HGX

hints: Every letter of the sentence was shifted along the alphabet by the same amount. Find the shift; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with L.

puzzles.title: High Score
puzzles.flavor: Recovered from the shredder in the arcade. Somebody at least had the decency to note how long each word was.
hints: The sentence was cut into three-letter fragments (spaces removed) and alphabetised. Reassemble it using the word lengths; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with M.

puzzles.title: Warp Zone
puzzles.flavor: The hands aren't telling the time. They're waving.
hints: Each clock's two hands are the two arms of a flag-semaphore signaller (hand length doesn't matter).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Extra Life
puzzles.flavor: Six switches at a time, some pressed, some not.
hints: Six-bit strings: the k-th character is 1 if Braille dot k is raised (dots 1-2-3 down the left, 4-5-6 down the right).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with S.

meta.title: Meta: Insert Coin
meta.flavor: Everything in the arcade has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with A.
